title: Mumbai's Indian Accent Earns Spot on 50 Best Discovery's Global Hospitality Guide
excerpt: The acclaimed restaurant, known for reinventing Indian cuisine with modern techniques, joins an elite group of global dining establishments recognized for outstanding hospitality.
body:
• Mumbai's Indian Accent has been recognized on 50 Best Discovery's Global Hospitality Guide, placing it among the world's top dining destinations.
  • The restaurant, helmed by chef Manish Mehrotra, is known for reimagining traditional Indian dishes with contemporary techniques and global ingredients.
  • The recognition follows Indienne's recent expansion from Chicago to New York, signaling growing global appetite for elevated Indian cuisine.
  • Indian fine dining is experiencing a breakthrough moment worldwide, with more Indian restaurants earning international accolades than ever before.

Global Recognition for Indian Fine Dining

Indian Accent, one of India's most celebrated restaurants, has earned a place on 50 Best Discovery's Global Hospitality Guide, cementing Mumbai's position on the global fine dining map. The recognition places the restaurant alongside the world's most acclaimed dining establishments, from three-Michelin-star French houses to groundbreaking Nordic kitchens.

Chef Manish Mehrotra, who has led Indian Accent since its founding, has built his reputation on a deceptively simple idea: take the flavors and techniques of India's vast culinary traditions and present them with the precision and creativity of a modern tasting menu. The result is dishes like blue cheese naan, duck khurchan with paratha, and daulat ki chaat reimagined as a dessert — food that respects its roots while refusing to be bound by them.

A Breakthrough Moment for Indian Cuisine

The recognition comes during what many food critics are calling a golden era for Indian fine dining globally. Earlier this month, Indienne — Chicago's only Michelin-starred Indian restaurant — opened a second location in New York's Hudson Yards, while restaurants like Masque in Mumbai and Gaggan in Bangkok have earned their own international followings.

"Indian cuisine has always been complex and sophisticated. The world is finally catching up."

— Manish Mehrotra, Chef, Indian Accent

For decades, Indian food abroad was largely confined to curry houses and buffet restaurants, often perceived as inexpensive comfort food rather than high cuisine. That narrative has shifted dramatically in the past five years, driven by a new generation of Indian chefs who trained in the world's best kitchens before returning to reimagine their own culinary heritage.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For the Indian diaspora, the growing recognition of Indian cuisine at the highest levels carries both pride and practical significance. As Indian restaurants earn Michelin stars, James Beard nominations, and spots on global best lists, the perception of Indian food in Western markets is fundamentally changing. This shift opens doors for Indian-origin restaurateurs and food entrepreneurs across the United States, United Kingdom, and beyond.

Indian Accent previously operated a location in New York's Midtown before the pandemic forced its closure. The Mumbai flagship's continued international recognition keeps the possibility of a return to the US dining scene alive.

What's Next

The 50 Best organization's Discovery platform serves as a pipeline to its prestigious annual World's 50 Best Restaurants list. A strong showing on Discovery could position Indian Accent for an eventual ranking among the world's top 50, a feat no Indian restaurant has yet achieved. With the country's culinary scene attracting unprecedented global attention, that milestone may not be far off.
nri_angle: Growing global recognition of Indian cuisine raises profile for diaspora restaurateurs and shifts perception of Indian food in Western markets.
